title: 2025 HMMT February Guts Problem 11
statement: Let \(f(n) = n^{2} + 100\) . Compute the remainder when \(f(f(\dots f(f(1))\dots))\) is divided by \(10^{4}\) .

solutions.text:
We claim that \(f^{k}(n)\equiv 1 + 100(2^{n} - 1)\bmod 10^{4}\) . We can see this by induction, as

\[f(1 + 100(2^{n} - 1)) = (1 + 100(2^{n} - 1))^{2} + 100\] \[\qquad \equiv 1 + 200(2^{n} - 1) + 100\pmod {10^{4}}\] \[\qquad \equiv 1 + 100(2^{n + 1} - 1)\pmod {10^{4}}.\]

Thus, it suffices to compute \(2^{2025}\bmod 100\) . We note that \(2^{2025}\equiv 0\) (mod 4) and by Euler's Totient theorem, \(2^{2025}\equiv 2^{5}\) (mod 25), so \(2^{2025}\equiv 32\) (mod 100). Hence, we can compute

\[f^{2025}(1)\equiv 1 + 100(31)\equiv \boxed {3101}\bmod 10^{4}.\]
